name: Pricing Page: Annual vs Monthly Emphasis
hypothesis: Emphasizing annual plans with 30% discount will increase customer lifetime value by 25%
description: Test whether highlighting annual plans (with 30% discount) as the default/recommended option increases annual subscriptions and overall LTV compared to current monthly emphasis.

variants.name: Monthly Emphasis (Current)
variants.description: Current pricing page with monthly plans as default

variants.name: Annual Emphasis
variants.description: Redesigned pricing page emphasizing annual plans

metrics.name: ltv_30day
metrics.description: Customer lifetime value projection based on 30-day cohort

metrics.name: time_to_decision
metrics.description: Time from landing on pricing to purchase

guardrails.description: Pause if overall conversion drops below 8%

targetingRules.description: Only show to new visitors (not existing customers)
Exclude partnership and enterprise leads (custom pricing)

expectedResults.description: Based on industry benchmarks and our A/B test of discount size, we expect annual plan adoption to increase from 25% to 35-40%, driving a 20-25% increase in LTV. Overall conversion may decrease slightly (2-3%) due to higher upfront cost, but LTV gains should far exceed conversion loss.

treatment.description: Expected: 38% annual, 3% conversion drop, 26% LTV increase

revenueProjection.description: $636K additional annual revenue if treatment wins

conditions.requirement: Treatment must increase LTV by at least 15%
conditions.description: LTV lift must justify any conversion rate drop

conditions.requirement: Conversion rate must not drop more than 5%
conditions.description: Can't sacrifice too much volume for higher LTV
Annual customers must stick around (validate commitment)

decisionMatrix.ship_treatment: LTV up 15%+, conversion drop <5%, churn stable, p<0.05
decisionMatrix.test_hybrid: Strong results but segment-dependent (e.g., good for B2B, bad for B2C)
decisionMatrix.continue_testing: Trending positive but need more data on retention

stages.name: Initial Test
checkpoints: Initial conversion and annual rate data
stages.description: A/B test to measure immediate impact

stages.name: Retention Analysis
stages.description: Wait 30 days to measure retention and validate LTV projection

stages.name: Full Rollout
stages.description: Roll out to 100% if all metrics positive

cohortTracking.description: Track cohorts for 90 days to measure long-term retention and LTV

segments.name: B2C

segmentation.analysis: Analyze results by segment to inform future targeting and personalization

estimatedImpact.description: Significant revenue and LTV opportunity with improved cash flow

references: Industry benchmark: Annual adoption increases 15-25% with emphasis
Previous experiment: 30% discount performed better than 20%
Competitor analysis: Most SaaS companies emphasize annual

risks.risk: Lower cash flow in short term if conversions drop
risks.mitigation: Monitor daily revenue and pause if drop is too severe

risks.risk: Annual customers may have higher expectations
risks.mitigation: Track NPS and support tickets by plan type

metadata.notes: This is a high-stakes experiment that could significantly impact revenue and LTV. Plan to run for full 30 days to capture retention data before making final decision. If successful, consider A/B testing different discount levels (25%, 35%) to optimize further.
